character: One dry Kiwi storyteller (Cam S, ElevenLabs voice 53CG2aO2HU48thT3QnMl, eleven_v3) talking a mate, a small Auckland developer doing four townhouses, through his programme in the second person: 'your spreadsheet', 'your buyer'. General NZ accent, never a caricature, no announcer lift, no exclamation marks. The cold open is deadpan (the spreadsheet as the keenest worker on the job), 'Congratulations' bone-dry, the product lines plain. Continuous speech: the narration never stops for more than 1 s; short beats for a laugh only.

settings.note: v3 only accepts stability 0.0 / 0.5 / 1.0; no style/speed/similarity

take.method: ONE unbroken request to /v1/text-to-speech/53CG2aO2HU48thT3QnMl/with-timestamps?output_format=mp3_44100_128 (model eleven_v3, stability 0.5); never sliced; laid onto the master at 0.0 s at gain 1.15 with tools/mux (no bed). Regenerated 2026-10-10 for the owner pronunciation fix (CTA "dot Co dot N Z"): attempt 1 kept as take-attempt1.mp3 (slower read), attempt 2 is take.mp3. The 2026-10-06 "dot co" takes are in archive-2026-10-06-co/.
take.stt_check: tools/el.py stt 2026-10-10: every word heard; only homophones/spellings differ (Labor/Labour, program/programme, poor/pour, gray/grey, Hand over/Handover, QSME as "QSME"/"QS Me", the CTA as "qsme.co.nz"/"qsme.koh.enz", i.e. "koh" said as KO).
take.max_gap_note: the longest gap is the scripted [short pause] laugh beat before "It was always February." (1.35 s); every other gap is at most 0.53 s (between "spreadsheet." and "Worked")

continuous_read_v3:
[dry] Only one on your job working Christmas Day? Your spreadsheet.

Worked Labour Day. Boxing Day. New Year's. Didn't even go to the bach. Handover the fifteenth. She'll be right.

Same job in Queue Ess Mee. Shutdown's on by default; we switched it off. Switch it back on. Only four of those days are public holidays. Your spreadsheet called the rest working days. Move them off, and there's your real finish. Congratulations. Your finish date just got later. [short pause] It was always February.

A finish date you can still say out loud in January. Sign up at Queue Ess Mee dot Co dot N Z.
